title: Run of the canonical-bit scan machine
statement: Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $i<k$ be a work-tape index, let $\alpha$ be a Boolean input word, and let $w$ assign a Boolean word to each of the $k$ work tapes. Starting from the configuration with state $(\mathrm{fwd},\mathrm{true})$, input head at position $1$, those tape contents, all work-tape heads at position $0$, and empty output, the canonical-bit scan machine reaches after exactly $2|w_i|+2$ steps the configuration with state $(\mathrm{done},c)$, the same tape contents and otherwise the standard initial configuration data, where $c$ is true precisely when the last symbol of $w_i$ (or true if $w_i$ is empty) is true. At every earlier time $t<2|w_i|+2$, its state is not $(\mathrm{done},b)$ for any Boolean value $b$.
hypotheses_covered: $w$ assigns a Boolean word to each of the $k$ work tapes
